content.user_title: Build Structured Python Logging with structlog
content.value_statement: Python logging configurations can become inconsistent across development, production, and tests. This skill provides practical structlog patterns for context, processors, output formats, exceptions, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Creates basic structlog processor pipelines for Python applications.
Shows JSON and console rendering configurations for different environments.
Integrates structlog with the Python standard logging module.
Demonstrates persistent request context through bound loggers.
Adds custom processors and structured exception formatting.
Tests emitted events with pytest and structlog LogCapture.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not install packages or execute application code.
Some snippets require additional imports and adaptation before use.
Does not define compatibility for specific structlog or Python versions.
Does not provide a complete policy for sensitive data redaction.

use_cases.title: Add Structured Application Logs
use_cases.description: Create a clear starting configuration with contextual fields and readable development output.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production JSON Logs
use_cases.description: Design processor pipelines that produce machine-readable events for centralized log systems.

use_cases.title: Verify Logging Behavior
use_cases.description: Capture structured events in pytest and assert expected messages and context.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal structlog configuration for my Python application. Use readable console output and show one contextual log event.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small Python service

prompt_templates.title: Configure Production JSON
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production structlog configuration with JSON output, timestamps, log levels, exception details, and bound request context.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate and Test Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate structlog with Python standard logging, then outline pytest assertions for message, level, request identifier, and exception fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Migration from standard logging with test coverage

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my logging requirements and propose development and production processor chains. Include ProcessorFormatter, context variables, redaction boundaries, performance choices, and testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for a high-throughput service

output_examples.input: Configure readable local logging and machine-readable production logging.
output: Development uses colored console rendering with timestamps and levels.
Production uses JSON rendering with request context and structured exceptions.
Both environments share a common processor chain before final rendering.

output_examples.input: Explain how to test a bound request identifier.
output_examples.output: Capture the emitted event with LogCapture, then assert that its message and request identifier match the expected values.

output_examples.input: Recommend context fields for an HTTP service.
output: Bind a request identifier when request processing starts.
Add stable service and operation names where they improve filtering.
Exclude credentials, tokens, and unnecessary personal data.

best_practices: Configure structlog once during application startup.
Bind stable request context early and avoid sensitive values.
Use readable console output locally and structured JSON in production.
anti_patterns: Do not configure processor chains separately in every module.
Do not log secrets, credentials, or unrestricted personal data.
Do not assume example snippets contain every required import or project setting.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It covers processors, renderers, context binding, standard logging integration, exceptions, performance settings, and test capture.

faq.question: Can it produce JSON logs?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates JSONRenderer configurations for machine-readable structured events.

faq.question: Does it work with Python standard logging?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows LoggerFactory, BoundLogger, ProcessorFormatter, and standard logging handlers.

faq.question: Can I test logging output?
faq.answer: Yes. The testing pattern uses pytest fixtures and LogCapture to inspect emitted event fields.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands or modify my project?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation examples and does not include scripts or command execution.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Add required imports, confirm version compatibility, set appropriate levels, test performance, and define sensitive data redaction.
